basics.name: Tishya Chhabra
basics.label: Computer Science Student
basics.summary: Dedicated computer science student with research experience applying data science and computer vision to coastal resilience, AI for healthcare, and programmable matter, along with prior experience in software engineering and robotics.

education.institution: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Honolulu, HI

work.summary: Growing Islands Project — tracking shoreline evolution on small sandy islands using satellite imagery and geospatial foundation models.
highlights: First-authored and presented workshop papers at NeurIPS and ACM KDD (2025); also presented at Coastal Geotools Conference (Jan 2025) to NOAA, FEMA, and USGS professionals.
Assisted in a presentation to the UN General Assembly, September 2024.

work.company: Hawaiʻi Digital Health Lab, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
work.summary: Evaluated the utility of Fitbit data combined with EHR data (NIH All of Us dataset) to predict lifestyle-related diseases.
highlights: Trained XGBoost models with Bayesian optimization and 10-fold CV + bootstrapped sampling for Type 2 Diabetes, Chronic Respiratory Disease, and Cardiovascular Disease.
Authored a first-author paper submitted to the Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing.

work.company: Self-Organizing Particle Systems Lab, Arizona State University
work.summary: Designed and implemented algorithms for programmable matter in the lab's particle simulator (Qt/C++).
highlights: Co-authored 2 conference publications on leader election and energy-constrained distribution algorithms (OPODIS 2023, ICDCN 2023).
Co-created a Dynamic Networks simulator using Java and GraphStream.

projects.name: FRC Robotics Team 6479
highlights: Manufactured, assembled, wired, and programmed teleoperated and autonomous routines for a 120-lb competition robot.
Led a 20-person team through a full competition season, from planning through milestone tracking.

projects.name: Global Innovation Challenge (Swish! Connect)
highlights: Led design of an auto-adjusting basketball hoop for special-education students, plus a companion app and website.
Programmed a ball-detection algorithm using OpenCV and Python.
Named Top 20 Finalist out of 884 international teams.
